methods: Firecrawl scrape of https://www.modo.com.ar/promos twice, ~30 min apart
Wayback CDX API query for 2026-01-01 to 2026-04-18 archived /promos/* URLs
modo.com.ar/sitemap.xml (4,492 total promo URLs including historical)

same_day_churn.verdict: ZERO churn in 30 min. Hub cache is stable same-day. This matches expectations (MODO publishes new promos monthly, not hourly).

wayback_2026_vs_live.verdict: The 2 sticky slugs validate the 'permanent program' category — the 'mar24' suffix on farmacias BNA has stayed alive for 2+ years. The other 29 archived slugs are MONTHLY promos that rotated out.

monthly_rotation_evidence.verdict: Monthly rotation CONFIRMED. Each month the slug suffix changes. The slug-diff strategy (detect new/changed slugs between daily hub crawls, re-extract only those) WILL WORK.

sitemap_signal.sitemap_lastmod_note: All 4,492 URLs share 6 nearly-identical lastmod timestamps (all within 4ms of each other, all 2026-04-18T20:33:34.xxxZ). Sitemap is regenerated as a bulk job; lastmod is NOT per-page content-change signal. Don't rely on sitemap lastmod for incremental refresh — use slug-set diff instead.

recommended_incremental_strategy.step_1: Daily hub scrape (~1 credit each for the 5 slot pages + root = 5 credits/day).
recommended_incremental_strategy.step_2: Diff today's slug set against yesterday's. New slugs → re-extract. Gone slugs → mark last_seen_at + TTL expire.
recommended_incremental_strategy.step_3: For existing slugs, content-hash the scraped markdown. If hash unchanged, skip LLM extract (save 25-30 credits per skip).
recommended_incremental_strategy.step_4: Monthly (1st of month): force re-extract of every active slug to catch legal-text changes the hash missed.
recommended_incremental_strategy.projected_credit_cost_daily_cadence: ~100 credits/day average (5 hub + ~3 new slugs × 30 credits) = 3k/month vs naive 45k/month full refresh.

wayback_limitations.finding: Wayback snapshots of the MODO hub capture ONLY the SPA shell (no JS rendered). Detail-page snapshots do exist (3csi-farmacias-bna-mar24 is there) but the rendered promo fields (tope, pct, Vigencia) are NOT in the captured HTML — same reason the live site requires Firecrawl to render. Wayback can prove a slug EXISTED at time T, but cannot validate its content state at T.
wayback_limitations.implication: We cannot backfill historical promo extractions from Wayback. If we need time-series data, we must start collecting it ourselves from day 1.
